# context API reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/documentation.cjs. Do not edit. -->

SPFx metadata access.

Instance identity is suitable for namespacing local state and diagnostics.

PageContext exposes metadata already supplied by the active SPFx host.

Consume registered services through the active native host scope.

## useSPFxContext

Returns static metadata for the nearest host-specific SPFx provider. Call inside a React component or hook; theme, size and property changes are exposed through dedicated runtime hooks. Although its implementation lives in an internal module, this hook is exported from the public hooks entry.

### Imports

```ts
import { useSPFxContext } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { useSPFxContext } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/hooks';
```

### Use when

- a descendant needs the native host context or instance identity without subscribing to runtime state.

### Throws

- Error when called outside a host-specific SPFx provider.

### Examples

#### Read Context metadata

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { useSPFxContext } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

function HostLabel() {
  const { kind, instanceId } = useSPFxContext();
  return <span>{kind}: {instanceId}</span>;
}
```

#### Inspect the current native host identity

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { useSPFxContext } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

type DemoRegions = { controls?: React.ReactNode; commands?: React.ReactNode; status?: React.ReactNode; diagnostics?: React.ReactNode; children?: React.ReactNode };
export function Demo({ render }: { render?: (regions: DemoRegions) => React.ReactElement; resetRevision?: number } = {}): React.ReactElement {
  const info = useSPFxContext();
  const regions: DemoRegions = {
    children: <dl aria-label="useSPFxContext result">
        <dt>Host kind</dt><dd>{info.kind}</dd>
        <dt>Instance ID</dt><dd>{info.instanceId}</dd>
        <dt>Native context available</dt><dd>{String(info.spfxContext !== undefined)}</dd>
      </dl>,
    diagnostics: <p>Provider metadata identifies this native host; mutable nested fields require a React render.</p>,
  };
  return render ? render(regions) : <>{regions.controls}{regions.commands}{regions.status}{regions.children}{regions.diagnostics}</>;
}
export const demo = { host: 'webPart', kind: 'snapshot', contentPlacement: 'configuration', observe: 'Inspect the actual Context values and explicit unavailable fields as the native host changes.' };
```

Returns static metadata from the nearest host-specific SPFx provider.
Call inside a React component or hook. Use dedicated runtime hooks for
reactive theme, property, display-mode and container-size state.

Returns:
- instanceId: Unique identifier for this SPFx instance
- spfxContext: The SPFx context object (WebPartContext, etc.)
- kind: Type of host component ('WebPart', 'AppCustomizer', etc.)

### Use when (2)

- a descendant needs the native host context or instance identity without subscribing to runtime state.

### Throws (2)

- Error if used outside an SPFx provider

### Examples (2)

#### Basic usage

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { useSPFxContext } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

function HostLabel() {
  const { kind, instanceId } = useSPFxContext();
  return <span>{kind}: {instanceId}</span>;
}
```

#### Render host metadata and guarded host-specific content

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { useSPFxContext, useSPFxInstanceInfo, useSPFxPageContext, useSPFxContainerInfo } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
function HostStatus() {
  const context = useSPFxContext();
  const instance = useSPFxInstanceInfo();
  const page = useSPFxPageContext();
  const container = useSPFxContainerInfo();
  const host = context.spfxContext;
  const root = 'domElement' in host && host.domElement instanceof HTMLElement ? host.domElement : undefined;
  const label = context.kind === 'WebPart' ? 'Full web part' : context.kind === 'AppCustomizer' ? 'Compact header' : 'Default host';
  return <section><h2>{label}</h2><p>{context.instanceId}: {context.kind}</p>
    <p>{page.web.title}: {page.web.absoluteUrl}</p><p>{page.user.displayName} {page.user.email}</p>
    <p>{page.cultureInfo.currentUICultureName}</p><p>{root?.tagName ?? 'No web-part root'}</p>
    <p>{container.size ? `${container.size.width}x${container.size.height}px` : 'No container'}</p>
    <button onClick={() => console.log(`[${instance.kind}:${instance.id}] Button clicked`)}>Log instance</button>
  </section>;
}
```

## useSPFxInstanceInfo

Returns static identity and host kind from the nearest provider. Use the identity to scope application storage or diagnostics; theme and property changes are exposed through their dedicated hooks. Call in a React component or hook beneath the matching host-specific SPFx provider.

### Imports (3)

```ts
import { useSPFxInstanceInfo } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { useSPFxInstanceInfo } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/hooks';
```

### Use when (4)

- an instance-scoped key or diagnostic entry needs the current provider identity.

### Throws (4)

- Error when no host-specific SPFx provider is present.

### Examples (5)

#### Read InstanceInfo metadata

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { useSPFxInstanceInfo } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

function InstanceLabel() {
  const { id, kind } = useSPFxInstanceInfo();
  return <span>{kind}: {id}</span>;
}
```

#### Inspect the provider instance identity

    children: <dl aria-label="useSPFxInstanceInfo result">
        <dt>Instance ID</dt><dd>{info.id}</dd>

## useSPFxPageContext

Consumes the host PageContext service lazily from the provider's ready ServiceScope and memoizes it for that consume function. Returns the host reference; it does not clone context, fetch list data or independently subscribe to every field mutation. Call in a React component or hook beneath the matching host-specific SPFx provider.

### Imports (4)

```ts
import { useSPFxPageContext } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { useSPFxPageContext } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/hooks';
```

### Use when (5)

- a descendant needs the native PageContext metadata instead of issuing a network request.

### Throws (5)

- Error when no host-specific SPFx provider is present.

### Examples (6)

#### Read PageContext metadata

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { useSPFxPageContext } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

function SiteLabel() {
  const context = useSPFxPageContext();
  return <span>{context.web.title}</span>;
}
```

#### Inspect selected native page metadata

export function Demo({ render }: { render?: (regions: DemoRegions) => React.ReactElement; resetRevision?: number } = {}): React.ReactElement {
  const info = useSPFxPageContext();
  const regions: DemoRegions = {
    children: <dl aria-label="useSPFxPageContext result">
        <dt>Web title</dt><dd>{info.web.title}</dd>
        <dt>Web URL</dt><dd>{info.web.absoluteUrl}</dd>

## useSPFxServiceScope

Reads the caller's SPFx dependency-injection scope and provides typed consumption. It does not create, register or finish services; consume follows the native ServiceScope lifecycle contract.

### Imports (6)

```ts
import { useSPFxServiceScope } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { useSPFxServiceScope } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/hooks';
```

### Use when (6)

- a component must consume an SPFx service registered in its host scope.

### Throws (8)

- When called outside an SPFx provider.

### Examples (8)

#### Basic usage (3)

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { useSPFxServiceScope } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

import { HttpClient } from '@microsoft/sp-http';

function ClientStatus() {
  const { consume } = useSPFxServiceScope();
  const client = consume(HttpClient.serviceKey);
  return <span>{client ? 'Client available' : 'Unavailable'}</span>;
}
```

#### Consume a registered service after native scope readiness

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { ServiceKey } from '@microsoft/sp-core-library';
import { PageContext } from '@microsoft/sp-page-context';
import { useSPFxServiceScope } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
interface ItemService { getData: () => Promise<string[]> }
class DefaultItems implements ItemService {
  public getData(): Promise<string[]> { return Promise.resolve(['Example item']); }
}
const itemKey = ServiceKey.create<ItemService>('example:Items', DefaultItems);
// The host owns custom registration/finishing; this key also supplies a native default implementation.
function ServiceItems() {
  const { consume } = useSPFxServiceScope();
  const [data, setData] = React.useState<string[]>([]);
  const [error, setError] = React.useState('');
  const page = consume(PageContext.serviceKey);
  React.useEffect(() => {
    let disposed = false;
    const service = consume(itemKey);
    service.getData().then(items => { if (!disposed) setData(items); })
      .catch(failure => { if (!disposed) setError(String(failure)); });
    return () => { disposed = true; };
  }, [consume]);
  return <section><h2>{page.web.title}</h2>{error && <p role="alert">{error}</p>}
    <ul>{data.map((item, index) => <li key={index}>{item}</li>)}</ul>
  </section>;
}
```
